title: Getting interested in music; playing 'bass' on a chair
summary: His father's friends held music evenings; as a boy he imitated a bass by rubbing a chair, then was bought a clarinet after years on drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, we were living back on Seals Avenue and my dad and a bunch of fellas used to get together every Thursday and they'd send to New Orleans and get a half-cag of beer. He'd buy it one Saturday and then the other fellas would buy it. They'd go around the circus like that one Saturday. And they had a band by the name of Tunson's. Used to come out here just to Rojas. Just take a trip and come out here in Rojas when he was coming out to his office. But they were strictly musicians. They didn't play nothing unless they had the music in front of me. And I used to get me a round out of a chair like that. With my finger and rub it across and it sounded like a bass. While they was playing I'd be sitting down on a coach or somewhere playing my bass on my fingers. But that got me in the rest of the music. What you mean, just lick your finger and rub it on that? No, lick my finger like that and rub that around that chair cause I found that bass. Yeah? Yeah, it sounded like a bass. If my finger went out, I wouldn't root it on that.
No, you gotta have that rod off that thing in your hand. Of course you couldn't just rub it on the hand.
Yeah, yeah. Yeah, somebody asked us something about that.
Yeah, somebody asked us something about that. Yeah, I was a little bit of a bass.

Yeah, I used to do that all the time. Alright. So, after I played drums with him for three, four years, and then he bought me a clarinet.
